cards.text: In a fair coin toss, each side has a one-in-two chance. Can I still lose on this single toss?
cards.rationale: Distinguishes the probability of an outcome from the result of one toss.
cards.alternative: The wording or swipe direction may have been misunderstood.
cards.effect: Yes opens the trade-off questions. No or Skip opens C02.

cards.text: After three wins in a row, can I still lose on a fourth, independent toss?
cards.rationale: Checks understanding after a neutral rephrasing.
cards.alternative: Persistent misunderstanding makes an aversion bound uninterpretable.
cards.effect: Yes unlocks the gambles. Otherwise φ stays undetermined.

options.no: No, it will be a win

cards.text: If my expenses were already covered, I would accept large swings in the value of my investments.
cards.rationale: Separates stated comfort with volatility from financial loss capacity.
cards.alternative: “Large” may suggest different amounts to different people.
cards.effect: Yes indicates greater stated comfort; No indicates less. Neither adds points.

cards.text: Would a temporary loss of CHF 2,000 on CHF 10,000 change your answer?
cards.rationale: Anchors stated tolerance to a monetary loss.
cards.alternative: The amount may change perceived risk or available cash.
cards.effect: Yes invites a review of T01. No retains the initial statement.

cards.text: Can you compare two hypothetical investments that each tie up CHF 1,000 for a year, assuming you will not need that money for expenses?
cards.rationale: Checks whether the certain payment and the gamble are comparable for this respondent.
cards.alternative: Needing the money could explain a preference for certainty.
cards.effect: Yes permits the gambles if the probabilities are understood. No or Skip leaves φ unbounded.

options.no: No, the comparison is a problem.

cards.text: If you invested CHF 1,000 for one year, would you prefer a guaranteed CHF 1,020 to an equal chance of ending up with CHF 900 or CHF 1,200?
cards.rationale: Under the mean–variance model, equal utility sets a bound on φ.
cards.alternative: A small hypothetical stake can elicit a different response from an entire household portfolio.
cards.effect: Right adds a lower bound; left adds an upper bound. Skipping adds neither.

cards.text: If you invested CHF 1,000 for one year, would you prefer a guaranteed CHF 1,000 to an equal chance of ending up with CHF 900 or CHF 1,200?
cards.rationale: Under the mean–variance model, equal utility sets a bound on φ.
cards.alternative: A small hypothetical stake can elicit a different response from an entire household portfolio.
cards.effect: Right adds a lower bound; left adds an upper bound. Skipping adds neither.

cards.text: If you invested CHF 1,000 for one year, would you prefer a guaranteed CHF 1,040 to an equal chance of ending up with CHF 900 or CHF 1,200?
cards.rationale: Under the mean–variance model, equal utility sets a bound on φ.
cards.alternative: A small hypothetical stake can elicit a different response from an entire household portfolio.
cards.effect: Right adds a lower bound; left adds an upper bound. Skipping adds neither.

cards.text: These choices are inconsistent under the model. Do you confirm that these were the answers you intended?
cards.rationale: Checks for input errors before retaining conflicting bounds.
cards.alternative: The model may not represent the respondent’s choices well.
cards.effect: Yes retains the contradiction. No invites correction of the gambles. Neither adds a bound.

cards.text: Your stated comfort with risk and your choices in the gambles suggest different attitudes. Would you like to review your statement?
cards.rationale: Compares stated comfort and gambling choices qualitatively.
cards.alternative: The stakes and context differ.
cards.effect: Yes reopens T01. No retains both observations separately.

cards.text: When assessing a loss, is the amount you originally invested the first reference point that comes to mind?
cards.rationale: Identifies the respondent’s stated reference point.
cards.alternative: A previous peak or a financial goal could also serve as the reference.
cards.effect: Record the stated reference. If probabilities are understood, the following pairs test sensitivity to framing.

cards.text: Starting with CHF 1,000, would you prefer a guaranteed CHF 1,000 to an equal chance of ending up with CHF 900 or CHF 1,100?
cards.rationale: Compares two economically equivalent descriptions at the same stake.
cards.alternative: Attention, framing or a mistaken swipe could change the answer.
cards.effect: Compare L01 with L02 and L03 with L04. These cards add no numerical bound.

cards.text: Here is the same choice expressed as a change in value. Would you prefer a guaranteed zero gain to an equal chance of losing or gaining CHF 100?
cards.rationale: Compares two economically equivalent descriptions at the same stake.
cards.alternative: Attention, framing or a mistaken swipe could change the answer.
cards.effect: Compare L01 with L02 and L03 with L04. These cards add no numerical bound.

cards.text: Starting with CHF 2,000, would you prefer a guaranteed CHF 2,000 to an equal chance of ending up with CHF 1,800 or CHF 2,200?
cards.rationale: Compares two economically equivalent descriptions at the same stake.
cards.alternative: Attention, framing or a mistaken swipe could change the answer.
cards.effect: Compare L01 with L02 and L03 with L04. These cards add no numerical bound.

cards.text: For that same CHF 2,000 investment, would you prefer no change in value to an equal chance of losing or gaining CHF 200?
cards.rationale: Compares two economically equivalent descriptions at the same stake.
cards.alternative: Attention, framing or a mistaken swipe could change the answer.
cards.effect: Compare L01 with L02 and L03 with L04. These cards add no numerical bound.

cards.text: Your answers differ depending on how the choices were presented at both investment sizes. Would you like to review them together?
cards.rationale: Two reversals justify a clarification.
cards.alternative: A reversal alone does not establish loss aversion.
cards.effect: Yes invites a review of both pairs. No records a framing observation.

cards.text: Your investments have just fallen by 15%. Would you consider selling now?
cards.rationale: Distinguishes three possible reasons for selling.
cards.alternative: Cash needs, discomfort and market expectations can coexist.
cards.effect: Yes opens the three follow-up questions about motives. No records an intention to stay invested.

cards.text: Would you sell to pay an expense?
cards.rationale: Uses a neutral follow-up to identify a motive for selling.
cards.alternative: More than one motive may apply.
cards.effect: No rules out this stated motive. Yes points to the cash flows in F03. The reserve is unchanged.

cards.text: If your bills were covered, would discomfort with this loss still be enough to make you sell?
cards.rationale: Uses a neutral follow-up to identify a motive for selling.
cards.alternative: More than one motive may apply.
cards.effect: No rules out this stated motive. Yes records a preference for stability. The reserve is unchanged.

cards.text: Would you sell because you expect a further fall?
cards.rationale: Uses a neutral follow-up to identify a motive for selling.
cards.alternative: More than one motive may apply.
cards.effect: No rules out this stated motive. Yes records a market view to discuss. The reserve is unchanged.

cards.text: If you stayed invested, would you like to compare a portfolio with an explicit hedge?
cards.rationale: Distinguishes hedging from selling the position.
cards.alternative: The cost of protection may change the choice.
cards.effect: Yes records a preference to compare a hedge. No leaves that preference inactive.

cards.text: If it took longer to reach your target amount, could you postpone your target date?
cards.rationale: Distinguishes a firm deadline from a preferred date.
cards.alternative: The feasible delay depends on the goal.
cards.effect: Yes opens H02. No records the date as a firm deadline.

cards.text: Would you also accept a lower target amount?
cards.rationale: Distinguishes flexibility in the target date from flexibility in the target amount.
cards.alternative: The minimum acceptable amount may need clarification.
cards.effect: Record the preference. F05 remains the source of the target amount.

cards.text: Would you like frequent updates on the value of your investments?
cards.rationale: Asks how often the respondent wants to check their investments.
cards.alternative: Frequent checks may simply reflect curiosity.
cards.effect: Yes opens S02. No records a preference for less frequent monitoring.

cards.text: Would a risk alert be enough between scheduled reviews?
cards.rationale: Distinguishes risk alerts from scheduled updates.
cards.alternative: A personal event may explain the preference.
cards.effect: Record the monitoring preference. It has no effect on φ.

cards.text: Would you like to track the individual portfolios in your blend separately?
cards.rationale: Identifies the level of detail required to monitor a blend.
cards.alternative: The answer determines no portfolio weights.
cards.effect: Record whether individual component portfolios should be visible.

cards.text: How much money do you have available today, in CHF?
cards.rationale: Establishes available capital.
cards.alternative: A range expresses uncertainty.
cards.effect: Keep both bounds before deducting the reserve.

cards.text: Until what date must this capital cover your expenses?
cards.rationale: Sets the time horizon for liquidity needs.
cards.alternative: The protection horizon may end before the target date.
cards.effect: Include flows on this date when calculating the reserve.

cards.text: What withdrawals and contributions do you expect? Add each cash flow, including those that are still uncertain.
cards.rationale: The cumulative shortfall at each date determines the reserve needed.
cards.alternative: An uncertain or late contribution might never be available when needed.
cards.effect: Count only confirmed contributions. Protect confirmed withdrawals and show the range of possible expenses.

cards.text: What size of financial loss, in CHF, would put your goal at risk?
cards.rationale: Measures stated financial loss capacity.
cards.alternative: A financially affordable loss may still be uncomfortable.
cards.effect: Keep the CHF range separate from emotional comfort with losses.

cards.text: What amount do you want to reach, and by what date?
cards.rationale: Records the goal before calculating the required return.
cards.alternative: The target date or currency may still be open.
cards.effect: Keep the amount bounds, currency and date.

cards.text: What annual return would you like on your CHF investment sleeve?
cards.rationale: Records the desired annual return.
cards.alternative: The desired return may exceed what is feasible.
cards.effect: Store the signed annual percentage range.

cards.text: How would you like to express your risk target?
cards.rationale: Distinguishes minimum risk, a volatility ceiling and a target band.
cards.alternative: An open preference needs confirmation after the scenarios.
cards.effect: Keep the request type and whether it applies to the sleeve or household for section 3.

cards.text: What annual volatility ceiling would you accept, as a percentage?
cards.rationale: A ceiling permits any lower volatility.
cards.alternative: Volatility measures dispersion at an annual frequency.
cards.effect: Retain the respondent’s ceiling for confirmation in section 3.

cards.text: What range of annual volatility would you like to target?
cards.rationale: A band has both a lower and an upper bound.
cards.alternative: The available assets may make the requested band infeasible.
cards.effect: Retain both bounds of the request.

cards.text: What exposures do you already have outside this investment sleeve?
cards.rationale: Identifies household concentrations outside the investment sleeve.
cards.alternative: Exposure to an employer may come from employment.
cards.effect: Keep the type, scope and description of each exposure.

cards.text: What diversification limits would you like to apply?
cards.rationale: Records diversification preferences by sector, country, currency or issuer.
cards.alternative: The requested scope or data coverage may be unknown.
cards.effect: Keep each rule and its priority. Suspend its use if a mandatory rule cannot be verified.

cards.text: Which securities or exposures would you like to exclude?
cards.rationale: Records explicitly requested exclusions.
cards.alternative: The requested scope or data coverage may be unknown.
cards.effect: Keep each rule and its priority. Suspend its use if a mandatory rule cannot be verified.

cards.text: Which environmental criteria would you like to apply?
cards.rationale: Records the environmental criterion requested.
cards.alternative: The requested scope or data coverage may be unknown.
cards.effect: Keep each rule and its priority. Suspend its use if a mandatory rule cannot be verified.

cards.text: Which risks would you like protection against?
cards.rationale: Records the risk the respondent wants to hedge.
cards.alternative: The requested scope or data coverage may be unknown.
cards.effect: Keep each rule and its priority. Suspend its use if a mandatory rule cannot be verified.

cards.text: How would you like to combine multiple portfolios?
cards.rationale: Records preferences for combining portfolios.
cards.alternative: The requested scope or data coverage may be unknown.
cards.effect: Keep each rule and its priority. Suspend its use if a mandatory rule cannot be verified.
